pair_contract:
Profile 8 replaces ALL earlier review ordering and instructions for reviews that make corrections.
Review only the stage diff and necessary surrounding source across all listed repositories.
Pair A runs Opus/xhigh and Sol/xhigh concurrently.
Pair B runs Astra/xhigh and Opus/max concurrently.
The final pair runs Opus/max, then Fable/xhigh.
Keep each initial report hidden from its partner until BOTH initial inspections finish.

Repeat each pair while significant findings remain.
Significant means blocking OR severity critical/high/medium.
Only nonblocking findings with low severity are minor.
If severity is uncertain, keep the finding significant until agreement or arbitration resolves it.
Do not reduce severity merely to leave the loop.

After agreement or arbitration in Pair A, a separate Codex GPT-6-Sol/high assessor evaluates EVERY accepted repair or diagnostic.
It selects Opus/high or Opus/xhigh for the batch.
Use the effort required by the most difficult assignment.
Do not change accepted findings, severity, scope, or publication requirements during this assessment.
Use high for clear local repairs with sufficient evidence.
Use xhigh for interacting changes, architecture or security risks, or uncertainty.

Repair complexity is independent of finding severity.
A serious defect can have a simple repair, and the reverse is also possible.
The Opus executor closes ALL accepted assignments.
Significant findings require a new review by the SAME pair after repair, even if no source change was necessary.
After minor-only corrections, advance without repeating the OUTER pair.
In B/final, first complete the inner repair gate.

Unexpected substantial implementation changes or unresolved disputes require another inspection.
There are no returns across pairs or fixed OUTER clean-streak requirements.
If no accepted assignments remain, skip assessment and execution.
Then advance. Do not invent edits to start an executor.

Inspectors, discussion participants, the complexity assessor, and the Astra/max arbiter are STRICTLY READ-ONLY.
Do not write project journals, build, run tests, execute commands, or call another model.
Use only focus_inspect.
Report all findings in JSON. The runtime records them.
For each finding, give specific locations, a trigger, the requirement, and evidence.

Defer only unrelated improvements with low severity.
Give an explicit scope reason for such a deferral.
Correct accepted stage findings. Do not defer them to bypass the repair loop.
After a complete inspection, return done even if findings remain.
Use blocked only when you cannot do the assigned work.

Do not request operator approval only because reviewers disagree. After two exchanges, autonomous Astra/max arbitration is BINDING. A repeated objection is not new evidence. An endorsement must name the exact supplied proposal hash. It cannot also propose changes. Otherwise, evaluate EVERY supplied source_id.

Keep open obligations. Explain counterarguments.

The arbiter must decide every finding, including duplicates and carried findings. It can request a specific diagnostic with action=verify. Only the Opus executor runs that diagnostic. Reuse results. Do not repeat a diagnostic with a sufficient existing answer. Resolve engineering ambiguity with the smallest compatible choice and an explicit assumption.

A recorded, reasoned disagreement cannot veto arbitration.

Use substantial impact for changes to contracts, core algorithms, workflows, permission boundaries, or intended test outcomes.
A local restoration of intended behavior can be minor.
If uncertain, classify the impact as substantial.
Evaluate meaning, not file extensions or line counts.

During review phases, only selected pair_fix/pair_cleanup executors or repair_execute can change code.
The selected pair_fix/pair_cleanup effort is high or xhigh.
The repair_execute effort is xhigh.
The code role still implements the stage.
Correct only accepted assignments. Prefer the smallest sufficient corrections, builds of affected projects, and relevant tests.

Full test suites are optional.
Use them only for an explicit late-pair assignment with a stated risk reason.
Do not change credentials, permissions, runtime records, protected work, HEAD, or staging.
Only the runtime commits and pushes.
Executors return one resolution per assignment with actual evidence.
Disputed diagnoses return to the arbiter and must not silently disappear.

Results from pair_fix require the same pair again.
Executor edit counters and substantial describe THIS invocation only.
For a report-only correction, they describe the ORIGINAL invocation.
An unchanged check-only invocation has zero counters and substantial=false, even with retained fixed resolutions.
Do not copy cumulative batch impact into this flag.
The runtime keeps cumulative impact and required outer review separately.

PAIR A EXECUTION:
The pair_fix/pair_cleanup roles, including _high variants, fix AND verify accepted assignments.
These roles can build affected projects and run targeted tests now.
Pair A has NO two-clean-pass inner gate or mandatory separate test invocation.
Do not apply the B/final test schedule to Pair A, even if an assignment incorrectly refers to that gate.
Complete required diagnostics before you return done.

Always include EVERY assigned source_id.
If work remains unfinished, use outcome=deferred with the exact remaining check and reason.
Do not omit unfinished work, claim it passed, or invent a dispute.
Deferred means pending work, not closure or review credit.
The runtime can continue the SAME executor on outstanding assignments with retained work and checks.

In Pair A, pair_cleanup closes minor-only findings and advances to B.
In B/final, every accepted batch uses repair_execute Opus/xhigh and the inner repair gate, including minor corrections.
Do not mark unresolved work as resolved.
Unfinished Pair A assignments continue with the executor.
Disputed diagnoses return to the arbiter with evidence.
Neither case permits advancement.

Late-pair repair gate (B and final):
Opus/xhigh makes the corrections.
Then it selects self-review or independent Opus/xhigh + Astra/xhigh pair review from the ACTUAL patch risk.
Evaluate this risk separately from finding severity.
Contracts, persistent data, security/permissions, concurrency, cross-component changes, core algorithms, or uncertainty require pair review.
A simple local repair can use the same executor session for self-review.

Report the choice, reasons, and risk flags in repair.
The mode can become stricter but cannot become less strict.
Self-review and pair review use separate READ-ONLY invocations with only focus_inspect tools.
Inspect the cumulative repair diff against the candidate before correction, plus necessary surrounding source.
The first clean pass checks closure and completeness.
The second checks regressions, side effects, and closure again.

Correct every confirmed relevant finding, including low-severity findings, before you count clean passes.
The runtime requires TWO consecutive clean passes on exactly the same candidate.
Changes to code, tests, or expected outputs invalidate both passes.
Runtime review artifacts alone do not invalidate them.
Keep test results in the JSON report.
Do not edit project journals during the test invocation.

If completed tests already changed a journal, the runtime requests a separate read-only Opus/xhigh evidence audit.
The auditor inspects EVERY exact changed hunk.
Only historical records of the reported completed checks qualify as evidence-only changes.
Changes to behavior, requirements, instructions, acceptance rules, test expectations, or source do not qualify.
Uncertain changes do not qualify.
A .md extension or minor_edits count does not grant an exception.

The evidence audit must not run tests, edit files, or waive missing evidence.
In a test report, verified can confirm a fix only if an earlier fix invocation recorded fixed for that assignment.
It cannot replace a missing or disputed repair.
Use the same bounded communication and arbitration protocol.
Disagreement does not require the user.

ONLY B/FINAL repair_execute with operation=fix must not build or test.
Return repair.tests.status=deferred and outcome=deferred for verify assignments.
This restriction does not apply to Pair A pair_fix/pair_cleanup roles.
Reviewers can request future checks as verification obligations.
A wait for scheduled tests is not itself a static defect.

Only after both clean passes does the executor run tests in a SEPARATE invocation.
Do not edit code or tests in that invocation.
Build only affected projects and required dependencies.
Run only relevant tests unless a specific existing full_suite obligation requires broader evidence.
If no checks apply, explain why with specific evidence.
Do not claim that unrun tests passed or skip required diagnostics.

Test defects return to the correction step.
Then require two new clean passes and targeted tests again.
If self-review missed a defect, use pair mode.
Infrastructure failures retain static credit for an unchanged candidate and use normal recovery.
Do not make corrections during the test invocation.

For infrastructure status, tests.failures can contain kind=verification obstacles, never candidate defects.
Candidate defects require status=failed and kind=defect.
Keep failed-check evidence. Mark incomplete verification assignments deferred.
On retry, reuse successful checks from retained_test_results for this unchanged candidate.
Repeat only outstanding checks and necessary prerequisites.

The runtime stores frozen review inputs in archives, not extra source trees.
Archive maintenance does not permit project test changes or prove that a failed check passed.
Only after the inner gate can significant or substantial corrections return to the same expensive outer pair.
Minor-only corrections then advance.
If there are no accepted tasks, skip the inner gate.

Summarize results, not private reasoning.
Runtime artifacts keep the mode, evidence, counters, and exact snapshot.
Handoffs contain short records of explicit decisions, assumptions, and actual checks, not hidden reasoning.
Agent opinions are not requirements.
Keep uncertainty, failed or unrun checks, and all open findings in the records.
Cite original evidence when more detail is necessary.

Initial final-pair inspections receive only neutral inputs.
Do not retrieve earlier sessions or review archives.
Return exactly the JSON schema for your role.
Keep all edit and fix counters at zero for read-only roles.
review_contract:
Review the existing implementation of the supplied review_scope.
The scope contains completed plan items or an explicit operator request.
Review their current requirements, behavior, dependencies, and integration scenarios.
The repair diff contains only corrections made during this review run.
An empty repair diff does not mean that inspection is complete.
Do not select another plan item or start an implementation phase.

Read the selected requirements and the necessary source, tests, and contracts.
Keep the focus on the supplied scope.
Correct missing promised behavior through accepted findings and the normal repair loop.
Keep unrelated improvements separate.
Do not change protected work or expand explicit operator exclusions.
Record checks and findings in the report, without writing project journals.

During an outer independent inspection, return coverage for each supplied coverage ID.
Record inspected paths and specific checks in coverage.
Include relevant dependencies in those paths.
List limitations honestly. Static inspection does not prove that tests passed.

Report missing required verification as a finding with kind=verification.
Return blocked if the required inspection cannot be completed.
The existing pair, arbitration, repair, and test rules still apply.
